title: OpenAI ships configurable context compaction to the Python SDK for long-running agents
subtitle: A new compact_threshold parameter and a standalone compaction endpoint give developers direct control over how agent sessions summarize their own history mid-run.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI's Python SDK v3.42.0, released Oct. 31, exposes configurable context compaction for Responses API agents. Developers can now pass a context_management parameter with a compact_threshold on client.responses.create — when the running token count crosses the threshold, the server summarizes earlier turns in place and continues the agent run without client-side bookkeeping. A separate standalone /responses/compact endpoint handles stateless compaction for callers that want the summary without opening a session.

The feature matters because agent runs break where context breaks. Until this week, keeping a Responses-API agent alive past the model's context window meant hand-rolling your own summarizer, deciding what to drop, and threading the compacted state back into the next call. Doing that correctly — without losing tool-call results, structured outputs, or the chain of reasoning that made the agent coherent in the first place — is one of the hardest things in production LLM engineering. Moving it server-side, with a declared threshold, standardizes behavior that most teams were already building badly.

This fits a broader direction in the SDK layer. Anthropic shipped memory and compaction primitives in Claude's native agent framework earlier this year, and Google's Gemini SDK added session-level compaction with its Agent Builder update. OpenAI's version is the first to make the threshold a first-class request parameter rather than a server-side default, which is a meaningful choice: it lets developers tune for cost ceilings and task structure rather than inheriting a one-size-fits-all policy.

Takeaway for learners: if you are building anything agentic, context management is where most production failures hide. Before you reach for a bigger model, learn what compaction actually does to your tool-call trace — specifically which fields survive the summary and which get dropped. The gap between 'the demo works' and 'the agent works at hour three' is almost always this layer.
